Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Asset Management Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to John Smith, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Asset Management's Q3 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are David Johnson, Chief Executive Officer; Emily Carter, Chief Financial Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Investment Officer; Michael Lee, Head of Distribution; Lisa Chen, Head of Operations; and Robert Hayes, Head of Risk Management.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to David Johnson.

David Johnson: Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3 2024. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by exceptional net flows totaling $15.6 billion, our strongest quarterly inflow since Q4 2021, alongside robust fund performance across equity, fixed income, and alternatives amid favorable market trends like the S&P 500's 5.1% gain and post-FOMC rate cuts. Our AUM grew to $1.2 trillion.

Emily Carter: Thank you, David. From a financial perspective, Apex Asset Management delivered strong results in Q3 2024. Our revenue was $3.48 billion, representing a 22% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by higher management fees on expanded AUM, performance fees of $178 million up 32% quarter-over-quarter, and a favorable shift toward higher-margin passive and alternative products. Our expenses were $2.05 billion, resulting in net income of $650 million. Our expense ratio improved to 71% due to disciplined cost controls, efficiency programs capturing $40 million in savings, and operating leverage as AUM scaled faster than costs.

Turning deeper into the key drivers behind those record net flows of $15.6 billion, which marked organic AUM growth of about 4.2% quarter-over-quarter—outpacing the industry average of 2.8% per Morningstar Direct—this success came from strong fund performance, market tailwinds, and strategic initiatives unpacked by asset class, channel, and region. Fund performance was a core catalyst: 68% of our equity strategies outperformed benchmarks on a one-year basis, up from 52% last quarter, thanks to tactical overweights in quality growth amid AI and mega-cap tech rotations. Our $28 billion Apex Global Equity Fund beat the MSCI World Index by 320 basis points YTD at 12.4%, drawing $4.2 billion in inflows as retail shifted from value strategies. In fixed income, 74% beat the Bloomberg Aggregate Bond Index, with $3.8 billion into short-duration and IG corporates like our Apex Core Bond ETF as 10-year Treasury yields fell 45 basis points. Alternatives added $2.1 billion commitments to Apex Direct Lending Partners at 14.2% net IRRs amid demand for 9-11% yields.

Market trends amplified this: equity ETF inflows hit $7.5 billion, our low-cost Apex S&P 500 UCITS ETF grabbing 15% European large-cap share per ETFGI; bond flows surged 28% for us versus 22% industry-wide post-50 bps cuts. ESG flows reached $2.9 billion led by Apex Climate Transition Equity at 11.8% YTD versus 9.2% for MSCI World ESG Leaders, ahead of EU SFDR and CSRD via our ESG scoring integrated with Aladdin-like analytics—offset by $800 million outflows from non-ESG EM debt amid China issues.

Technical levers included three mutual fund-to-ETF conversions unlocking $1.5 billion seed, our model delivery marketplace with Envestnet and Orion driving $900 million RIA flows up 35% YoY, and Apex Wealth app adding $650 million via 45,000 retail accounts. North America led at $9.8 billion from 401(k)/IRA shifts up 7% per ICI; Europe $3.7 billion on UCITS; APAC $1.6 billion from HNW outflows; LatAm $500 million despite FX. Institutional $8.4 billion including $2.3 billion OCIO wins; retail $7.2 billion via wirehouses.

We're doubling down on active alpha in passive wrappers, targeting retirement flows with $20 billion pipeline, resilient with 60/40 positioning and $50 billion liquidity.

Before Q&A, let me provide forward-looking guidance for the second half of 2024 and into early 2025, assuming no major disruptions beyond VIX at 15 and stable regs. Full-year adjusted revenue $2.85 billion to $2.95 billion, 8-12% over 2023's $2.64 billion; Q3 $710-740 million, Q4 $740-770 million. Management fees ~85% on year-end AUM guide $560-580 billion with $20-25 billion H2 organic flows: $15-20 billion long-term led by U.S. institutional into Vista Core Equity up 250 bps vs. peers; $5-7 billion ETF/model like VISTA ESG Global Leaders at $12 billion up 45% YTD; $2-3 billion alts with $150-200 million performance fees skewed Q4. Fees steady 38-39 bps, offset by alts premium; other revenue $250 million up 5%. North America 65%, EMEA 25% with UCITS gains, APAC 10% accelerating.

Expenses $2.05-2.10 billion, 6-8% up, ratio 71-73% toward 68% target. Compensation/benefits $1.07-1.09 billion up 7% with $180 million variable at 4:1 fixed ratio; distribution/marketing $305-315 million flat with $50 million VistaOne AI; G&A/tech $365-375 million up 10% on cyber/cloud; occupancy/other $315-340 million with FX hedges. Efficiency Alpha saves $40 million YTD; EBITDA 22.5-23.5%, FCF $650 million for buybacks/dividend 2.8%. Upside from three active ETFs; resilient to Fed delays/China slowdowns.

On compensation ratio specifically, it was 42.3% this quarter—down 210 bps YoY from 44.4%, 80 bps better sequentially—marking seven quarters of improvement on $1.47 billion comp up 8% versus 22% revenue growth to $3.48 billion from fees, $320 million performance fees up 35%, passive mix. Base/benefits 18.2% flat at 4,200 headcount; variable annual 15.1% down from 17.8% tied to Sharpe/alpha/flows; LTIs 9.0% benchmarked to TSR. Americas 45.6% on talent wars, countered by retention; EMEA 38.2%, APAC 35.7%. ApexAI models comp to revenue attribution, cutting overpays 12%; RPA/genAI saves $150 million by 2026; scale ETFs dilute fixed costs. FY guide 42.5-43.0% to <40% by 2027, 150 bps below industry.

Operating expenses totaled $462 million, up 5.2% YoY flat sequentially, 35 bps on $515 billion avg AUM—below 38-40 bps target, competitive vs. peers. Compensation/benefits $248 million 54% up 4.1% on 2% headcount offset by cuts; variable $112 million at 105% target. Tech/data $72 million 16% up 12% on GAP AlphaCore AI/cloud $18 million, data $12 million, EMEA SFDR/APAC robo. Distribution/marketing $58 million 13% up 8% on inflows/sub-advisory; G&A $42 million 9% down 2% on savings; amortization/other $42 million 9% up 6% on acquisition/cyber. FY guide $1.85-1.90 billion, 36 bps ratio.

Performance fees $178 million Q4 up 32% QoQ/28% YoY, FY $612 million up 41%; 72% mandates above watermarks. Equities: U.S. Large Cap Growth 18.2% gross trail S&P 500 24.2% but net 17.1% beats post-fees, NVIDIA alpha 450 bps; Small Cap Value 12.8% beat Russell 2000. Int'l: Global Equity 15.4% +320 bps MSCI World ex-US, Europe +4.8% STOXX. Fixed: Core Bond 2.1% +350 bps Bloomberg Agg, Euro 1.8% +280 bps. Alts: L/S Equity 21.6% + HFRI, priv credit 11.2% IRR. Quant/ML/ESG enhancements.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Emily. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities and fixed income. We are navigating the current market environment by leveraging proprietary quant overlays, GenAI sentiment analysis scanning 10 million data points daily for 22% better earnings predictions, and dynamic asset allocation via our Economic Regime Model signaling late-cycle growth. We launched the Apex Multi-Asset Outcome Fund this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with strong interest from retail RIAs targeting defined outcomes against S&P 500 volatility.

Diving into fund performance relative to peers and benchmarks, in Q3 we delivered robust outperformance across most strategies on $285 billion AUM up 8% QoQ with $12.4 billion inflows. Core equities 52% AUM: Apex U.S. Large Cap Growth 14.2% net +320 bps Russell 1000 Growth, top decile vs. Fidelity/T. Rowe, Sharpe 1.85 vs. 1.42 peer median on NVIDIA/Microsoft AI. Int'l: Global Equity 9.8% +210 bps MSCI ACWI ex-US, Europe defensives + STOXX flat; EM Alpha 11.3% +290 bps MSCI EM. Fixed 28% AUM: Core Bond 4.1% +65 bps Bloomberg Agg first quartile vs. Vanguard/PIMCO; CLO 6.8% +140 bps JPM CLOIE. Alts 15%: Diversified 7.9% +290 bps HFRI, PE secondaries 18.2% IRR +450 bps Cambridge. Aggregate alpha 1.4% YTD, beta 0.92, active share 68%, tracking error 3.8%. ESG 95% coverage +80 bps; direct indexing $18 billion +45 bps tax-alpha. U.S. +250 bps, Europe +180 bps, APAC reallocated. Forward: equities 10-12%, FI 4-5%.

Michael Lee: Thank you, Sarah. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in APAC and Europe are paying off, as evidenced by partnerships driving $4.2 billion flows up 28% YoY, 45% of total for 16% AUM growth to $285 billion. Institutional/intermediary: wirehouses Morgan Stanley/UBS co-branded SMAs $1.8 billion Apex Core Equity; Envestnet/SEI models $2.1 billion up 35% at 45 bps fees. RIA 42% US assets: Schwab/Fidelity direct indexing $1.1 billion 92% retention via Apex Optimizer/Addepar API +22% conversions. DCIO: Empower white-label TDF $650 million 18-month duration. US 68%, Europe Deutsche Bank UCITS €1.2 billion MiFID, APAC DBS SGD 800 million ETF CAGR 15%, LatAm Itaú $200 million. Apex Direct B2B2C $450 million alts/robo, $25 million tokenization pilots. Target $20 billion 2025 inflows, 12-15% CAGR.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we've made significant progress in improving our technology infrastructure, including cloud migrations to AWS reducing latency 40%, AlphaCore AI rollout, and RPA automating 25% middle/back-office for $150 million savings by 2026. This has resulted in increased efficiency and reduced operational risk. We are also focused on cyber-resilience upgrades post-SEC Reg S-P, quantum-resistant encryption for tokenized pilots with Fidelity, and zero-based budgeting/vendor optimization harvesting $15 million efficiencies.

Robert Hayes: Thank you, Lisa. From a risk management perspective, we continue to maintain a robust framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across the organization. We have enhanced our monitoring of market volatility and geopolitical risks like US elections or inflation rebounds, and are taking steps to address potential vulnerabilities. This includes tighter tracking error controls to 2.8-3.8%, risk parity overlays, 60% ESG screens, and a $50 billion liquidity buffer alongside geographic diversification—Americas 62%, EMEA/APAC leaner comp/risk profiles.

David Johnson: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes scaling active alpha in passive wrappers, launching new active ETFs targeting AI infrastructure, direct indexing for 15 bps uplift, retirement super-cycle pipelines, and resilience via diversified channels and tech like ApexAI/Aladdin integrations.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Morningstar.

Alex Rivera: Good morning. Can you provide more details on drivers of net flows?

David Johnson: Thanks, Alex. Emily can provide more color.

Emily Carter: Happy to, Alex. As I detailed earlier, the $15.6 billion was propelled by 68% equity outperformance like Apex Global Equity's 320 bps beat, fixed income 74% ahead, alts IRRs, market rotations in Magnificent Seven and bonds post-cuts, ETF conversions, model marketplace, digital apps, with NA leading but APAC accelerating—positioned resiliently for Q4 volatility.

Alex Rivera: Thank you. And a follow-up on revenue and expense guidance?

Emily Carter: Sure. FY revenue $2.85-2.95 billion on $560-580 billion AUM, H2 flows $20-25 billion across long-term/ETF/alts, fees 38-39 bps; expenses $2.05-2.10 billion ratio 71-73%, comp up 7%, tech 10%, efficiencies offsetting—EBITDA 22.5-23.5% with FCF for capital returns.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jordan Patel with Bloomberg.

Jordan Patel: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of Apex Global Equity Fund?

Sarah Thompson: Good question, Jordan. As noted, it returned 12.4% YTD +320 bps MSCI World, Q3 9.8% +210 bps ACWI ex-US on Europe defensives and EM tilts—top decile peers, Sharpe superior, driving $4.2 billion flows.

Jordan Patel: And how is the new product Apex Multi-Asset Outcome Fund performing relative to expectations?

Michael Lee: Early days but exceeding: strong RIA commitments for S&P overlays at 10% vol budget, inflows aligning with targets via partnerships, capturing dispersion alpha as anticipated.

Operator: Our next question comes from Taylor Kim with Goldman Sachs.

Taylor Kim: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Lisa Chen: Absolutely, Taylor. Tech infra upgrades like AWS/AlphaCore cut latency 40%, RPA 25% automation saves $150 million run-rate, cyber enhancements, shared services—$40 million YTD savings, expense ratio down to 35 bps, supporting margin expansion.

Operator: Our next question comes from Chris Lopez with JPMorgan.

Chris Lopez: What are your thoughts on the current regulatory environment and its impact on your risk profile?

Robert Hayes: Thanks, Chris. Regs like SFDR/CSRD/MiFID II are tailwinds for our ESG/UCITS positioning, T+1 via automation mitigated; Dodd-Frank clawbacks intact. Risk framework enhanced with ML factor timing, low beta 0.92, diversified footprint caps exposures—profile stable, resilient to elections/inflation.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to David Johnson for closing remarks.

David Johnson: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
